# downpipe

> downpipe is the offline reference reader for the `downpipe/0.1.0` backup archive format. It is a single static MIT-licensed Go binary that recovers, verifies and attests an archive entirely offline, with no vendor, no network and no account. It is the recover-forever guarantee for the downpipes platform: even if the vendor, the console and the cloud account all vanish, a holder of the break-glass identity `identity.key` and a pinned operator signer can still read their data with this tool. The pinned signer is the recovery-kit file `signer.pub`, or (from reader 0.3.4) the signer fingerprint on the printed recovery sheet, which pins the bucket's copy of `signer.pub`. An engine writes that copy from 0.3.7, and it is always the current signer's key, so after a signer rotation the older runs still need the kit file.

The format itself is `downpipe/0.1.0`, semver'd (while the major is 0 a byte-level rule change bumps the minor and is a new, incompatible identity) and specified byte-for-byte in `docs/format/SPEC.md`. The tool versions independently under 0ver. Confidentiality and integrity are post-quantum hybrid (X25519 + ML-KEM-1024 for key encapsulation, Ed25519 + ML-DSA-87 for signatures), and content is sealed with AES-256-GCM. The post-quantum halves, AES-256 and SHA-384 use CNSA 2.0 parameters.

## Commands

- `downpipe keygen`: generate a break-glass recipient identity and a signer keypair.
- `downpipe inspect --archive <dir> --run <id>`: show a run's cleartext root manifest, no identity needed. `--run` is required; when the run id is not known, `downpipe keys --which --archive <dir>` lists the runs a source holds.
- `downpipe keys --which --archive <dir>`: group the runs a source holds by the recipient identity that opens them, no identity needed. With `--fingerprint` and the key files instead, it prints the fingerprints to check against a printed recovery sheet.
- `downpipe verify --archive <dir> --run <id> --identity <file> --signer <file>`: verify a run end to end against an identity and a signer. `--signer-fingerprint <fingerprint>` can replace `--signer`: the reader then uses the `signer.pub` copy in the archive's recovery bundle only if its fingerprint equals the value from the recovery sheet.
- `downpipe attest --archive <dir> --run <id>`: integrity check without an identity: shard hashes and RUNLOG, and the root signature when `--signer` is given. `--signer` is optional; without it the check is keyless.
- `downpipe verify-report --signer <file> --report <file>`: verify the signature on an assurance report the engine generated (restore tests, SLA compliance, immutability, posture, evidence pack or change records) against the signer public key, offline. The report is the JSON the engine returns, not the PDF, and `--report -` reads it from standard input. Both signature halves (Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87) must verify. `--signer-fingerprint <fingerprint>` checks the `--signer` file against the recovery sheet. Exit 0 means verified, 2 means the report is unsigned, changed, signed by another signer or carries a damaged signature, and 6 means the input is not a report JSON or a flag or key file is wrong.
- `downpipe restore --archive <dir> --run <id> --identity <file> --signer <file> --out <dir>`: plan the writes (dry run by default); pass `--apply` to write. A pinned signer is required, as it is for `verify`: `--signer` with `signer.pub` from the recovery kit, or `--signer-fingerprint` with the fingerprint from the recovery sheet. The bucket has no copy of `signer.pub` until an engine 0.3.7 or later writes to it, and after a signer rotation the copy is the new signer's. In those cases the file has to come from the recovery kit. `--out` is required for the default `--sink file`. Sinks are `--sink file` (one file per record under `--out`, plus a `<path>.downpipe-meta.json` sidecar that keeps a KV or R2 record's metadata), `--sink env` (dotenv lines), or `--sink discard` (decrypt-and-verify restorability check that writes nothing).
- `downpipe prune --archive <dir> --identity <file> --signer <file> --keep <n>`: plan, and with `--apply` delete, the runs a retention policy has superseded.
- `downpipe unseal-export --in <file> --sig <file> --signer <file> --identity <file>`: open a sealed control-plane export offline with a recovery kit.
- `downpipe recombine --share <file> --share <file> --share <file> --envelope <file>`: rebuild `identity.key` offline from an M-of-N custodian split. A `--share` file is the labelled share download or a file holding the bare share body a custodian received by email; `--wrapping-key <file>` replaces the shares when the whole key was stored. Local files only, no network.
- `downpipe selftest`: build and recover a sample archive end to end.
- `downpipe preflight --account <id>`: read-only deploy-time Cloudflare account checks, using your own `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. `--account` is required, and `--domain <name>` adds a check that the zone is active on that account.
- `downpipe setup`: provision Cloudflare from your own machine using your own `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (dry run by default; `--apply` to provision).
- `downpipe init`: print the ordered least-privilege deploy runbook (print only, no live call).
- `downpipe update`: print the scoped-elevate, deploy, revoke upgrade runbook (print only, no live call).
- `downpipe version`: print the tool version.

inspect, keys, verify, attest, restore and prune read from a local `--archive <dir>`, from an S3-compatible bucket via `--s3-endpoint`/`--s3-bucket` (credentials from `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), or from an Azure Blob container via `--azure-endpoint`/`--azure-container` (credentials from `AZURE_STORAGE_KEY` or `AZURE_STORAGE_SAS_TOKEN`). Azure Blob is not an S3-compatible store and is not reachable through `--s3-endpoint`, which is why it has its own pair. A destination that cannot be reached exits 11, which is never a verdict about the archive.

## Recovery path

The fastest path to your data: hold `identity.key` and either `signer.pub` or the signer fingerprint from your recovery sheet, point the tool at the archive, and run `verify` then `restore --apply`. Neither command starts without a pinned signer, so `identity.key` alone cannot recover. For a bucket with no copy, or a run sealed before a signer rotation, the pinned signer has to be the `signer.pub` file. The step-by-step recovery guide, including what to do when only the bucket survives, is in `docs/RECOVER.md`.

## Key documents

- [Format specification](docs/format/SPEC.md): the normative `downpipe/0.1.0` wire format. Never renamed.
- [Recovery guide](docs/RECOVER.md): how to recover an archive offline, start to finish.
- [Conformance vectors](docs/format/CONFORMANCE.md): the test vector corpus a clean-room re-implementation must pass.
- [JSON schema](docs/format/schema.json): a machine-readable schema for the manifest structures, secondary to SPEC.md.
- [README](README.md): build, install and quick-start.
- [Security policy](SECURITY.md): reporting and disclosure.

## Notes for tools

- The format identifier `downpipe/0.1.0` is exact and MUST NOT be paraphrased; a byte-level rule change ships as `downpipe/0.2.0`, never as an edit to 0.1.0.
- The binary is offline by design. `inspect`, `verify`, `attest`, `recombine` and `restore` make no call to the vendor and send no telemetry. Pointed at `--archive <dir>` they make no network call at all; pointed at `--s3-endpoint` or `--azure-endpoint` the only host they contact is the destination endpoint you named, which is the same file read over HTTPS.
- The only standing Cloudflare API token the running platform engine holds is the read-only discovery token an Owner sets for the account-wide sources. Deploy tokens are scoped, short-lived and deleted after use.
